states.narration: Read each x+2 as a whole group. The first term has three copies and the second has four copies of that same group.
Combine the two counts, in their original order. Keep the shared group x+2 on the right, with everything inside its parentheses unchanged.
Three plus four makes seven copies of x+2. Only the count was evaluated; x+2 still depends on x.

editorial.title: Count copies of the same group
editorial.setup: Look inside the two pairs of parentheses: both contain x+2. Treat that repeated sum as one unit while combining its copy counts.
editorial.summary: Three groups plus four identical groups gives seven groups. Collecting their coefficients preserves the entire sum x+2; it does not find the value of x+2.
